speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned you have blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces; can you tell me when these symptoms first appeared and if they are painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Captopril-induced Stomatitis and Bullous Pemphigoid. (Note: While the symptoms of mucosal ulcers and painful blisters are consistent with captopril-induced stomatitis, the specific presentation of blisters on the forearm alongside mucosal involvement raises suspicion for a drug-induced autoimmune blistering disease like Bullous Pemphigoid or Stevens-Johnson Syndrome. Given the medication change, the most likely primary cause is the new drug, but the blistering nature requires further clarification of the lesions' appearance to rule out severe cutaneous adverse reactions.)
